author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The U.S. federal budget deficit narrowed to $167 billion in August, but the Treasury Department said the change largely reflected calendar shifts rather than an underlying improvement. Medicare and Social Security payments normally made on August 1 were paid in July because the date fell on a Saturday.

After adjusting for those timing effects, the August deficit was $248 billion, $7 billion more than a year earlier. Unadjusted outlays fell 24% to $527 billion, while receipts rose 5% to $360 billion. Interest payments declined by $14 billion for the month because of inflation-accounting changes, even as fiscal-year-to-date interest costs remained 13% higher.

The deficit for the first 11 months of the fiscal year was about $1.97 trillion, already above the $1.775 trillion gap for all of fiscal 2025. Net customs receipts rose in August after tariff refunds, while year-to-date customs collections totaled $292.5 billion before $125.2 billion in refunds, according to Treasury data.
dek: Treasury data showed the 11-month fiscal gap holding near $1.97 trillion, already above the full-year 2025 deficit.
headline: U.S. August budget deficit narrows to $167 billion on timing shifts
